subject.title: [Feature]: Configurable auto-cleanup and archival policy for webhook/hook sessions

question: Should hook mappings support explicit persistent, cleanup-on-completion, and delayed-retention modes while retaining current persistent behavior as the compatibility default?
rationale: OpenClaw has valid disposable task-hook and persistent multi-turn-hook use cases, so defaults, transcript ownership, and precedence with generic maintenance require maintainer intent.

options.title: Add explicit lifecycle modes
options.body: Preserve current persistence by default and allow mappings to opt into completion or delayed cleanup with explicit transcript handling.

options.title: Use generic maintenance only
options.body: Avoid hook-specific configuration and address accumulation through session.maintenance, documentation, and session-list filtering.

options.title: Make hooks ephemeral by default
options.body: Automatically remove isolated hook sessions unless a mapping explicitly requests persistent history.

recommendation.title: Add explicit lifecycle modes
recommendation.body: Preserve current persistence by default and allow mappings to opt into completion or delayed cleanup with explicit transcript handling.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest evidence connects this person to both the current product discussion and hook session-key behavior.
